column1: # Four real repositories.  Each one catches a defect that THIS KB had already documented and
# that pass 16 re-imported anyway, in a classifier it wrote from scratch because this
# environment refused to execute compose/code/lib/probe_payload.sh ("code from external").
# Run ANY new licence instrument against these four BEFORE trusting one row of it.
# repo <TAB> branch <TAB> expected_family <TAB> payload_bytes <TAB> why this case is REQUIRED

column5: P299 / SUBSTRING. The warranty disclaimer contains "IMPLIED", which contains the substring "mpl". Any classifier testing `'mpl' in text` calls this MIT payload MPL-2.0 -- and this KB builds an architecture recommendation on richie being MIT, so the defect inverts a published recommendation. A licence token is a WORD or it is noise.

P171 / MENTION-NOT-TITLE. Line 18 of this GPL-2.0 payload reads "the GNU Lesser General Public License instead." A 40-line "title block" still contains the PREAMBLE, so an LGPL test that runs before the GPL test wins on a mention. Decide the family on the NAME LINE (first ~3 non-empty lines), never on a preamble.

CC0 BRANCH ORDER. The string "CC0 1.0 Universal" contains neither "creative commons" nor "cc by", so CC0 nested INSIDE a CC-BY gate is unreachable. lib/license_family.sh:120 has CC0 as its own EARLIER branch. Copying an architecture from prose does not copy its branch order.

SIZE FLOOR + REUSE. This 1001-byte file is a REUSE-spec POINTER, not a grant: the real text is LICENSES/LGPL-2.1-or-later.txt. A full LGPL-2.1 is 27030 bytes (cf. Tampere/trevaka). Any family whose canonical text is long must be rejected in a short file. UNCLASSIFIED is the CORRECT answer here -- refusing to guess is the pass condition.
